title: Architecture Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance (Consolidated)
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

This consolidated guidance defines Redwood Inference's architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure (IaC and networking), model-serving conventions, observability, and performance. The intent is to provide clear, actionable rules for new and existing services so teams can build predictable, maintainable, and reliable systems that meet our SLOs and operational expectations.

Scope
- Applies to all services and components that serve model inference, control plane APIs, the Console, and operational tooling.
- Excludes ephemeral prototype code in personal repos (see eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates for prototyping guidance).

Owners & Contacts
- Standards owner: eng-platform (primary contact: Ava Martinez)
- API design owner: eng-developer-experience (contact: Rohit Patel)
- Model-serving owner: eng-serving-runtime (contact: Sofia Nguyen)
- Observability owner: eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts (contact: Ethan Brooks)

High-level Principles
1. Production-first: prioritize reliability, observability, and repeatable operations over one-off optimizations.
2. Developer ergonomics: APIs and tools must be simple and consistent across products.
3. Cost-aware engineering: prefer designs that make unit economics measurable and controllable.
4. Safe defaults: secure and error-resilient defaults for new projects.

Standards by Area

1) API Standards
Purpose: Ensure API consistency across Redwood products (hosted API, console, control plane).
Key rules:
- Versioning: use explicit major version segment in paths: /v1/..., plan v2 for breaking changes.
- Resource-oriented paths: prefer nouns over verbs; example: POST /v1/models -> create model; GET /v1/models/{id}/versions -> list versions.
- Idempotency: write operations must be idempotent where possible. Provide Idempotency-Key header for long-running model operations.
- Status codes: 200/201 for success, 202 for accepted async work, 4xx for client errors, 5xx for server errors. Provide structured error body with fields: code, message, retryable (boolean), request_id.
- Pagination: cursor-based (limit, after_cursor). Do not use offset for large collections.
- Rate limiting: responses must include X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset. Default per-tenant tiering handled by gateway.
- Auth: OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens for user-facing APIs, mutual TLS or signed JWTs for inter-service control plane.
- Telemetry headers: pass X-Request-Id and X-Trace-Id from edge to backend; services must honor and log them.
- OpenAPI: every public API must publish an OpenAPI 3.0 spec in the repo under /api/openapi.yaml and kept in sync with tests.

Example API error JSON:
{
  "code": "MODEL_NOT_READY",
  "message": "Model is warming up, try again in 30s",
  "retryable": true,
  "request_id": "abc123"
}

2) Coding & Testing Standards
Purpose: Maintainable, secure, and testable codebase across services.
Rules:
- Languages and runtimes: default to Go for stateless services, Python for model/ML tooling, and TypeScript for frontend/console. Exceptions require a documented justification.
- Style & linters: enforce gofmt/golangci-lint for Go, black/flake8/isort for Python, and eslint + prettier for TypeScript.
- Unit tests: minimum 80% coverage for critical service packages; at least one unit test per public function.
- Integration tests: must run in CI against a reproducible test environment (Docker Compose or ephemeral test cluster). Use the shared test infra in eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build.
- Contract tests: all API services must publish consumer-driven contract tests for cross-team integrations.
- Secrets: never commit secrets. Use vault (see eng-infra/cloud-accounts-and-networking) and secret linting in CI.
- Dependency management: pin versions in go.mod, poetry.lock, package-lock.json. Review dependency updates with automated PRs and vulnerability scanning.
- Pull requests: PRs require at least one reviewer from owning team and passing CI. For changes that touch public APIs or infra, include at least one reviewer from eng-platform.

3) Infrastructure & IaC Standards
Purpose: Secure, consistent, and auditable infrastructure deployments.
Rules:
- IaC: Terraform for cloud infra; modules must live under infra/terraform/modules and follow naming/tagging conventions.
- State: remote state stored in encrypted S3 and locked with DynamoDB (or cloud equivalent).
- Tagging: all resources must include tags: team, project, environment, cost-center.
- Network: default VPC segmentation: control-plane (private), public ingress (edge), and customer-dedicated (for Private). Use least-privilege security groups.
- Secrets management: KMS for envelope encryption, Vault for dynamic secrets, and HSM where required for FIPS workflows.
- Change management: require PR-based plan review, automated drift detection, and a change approval step for production (see policies-and-process/change-management).
- Observability & alerting hooks: infra modules must expose observability outputs (metric namespaces, log group names) for downstream dashboards.

Example Terraform module metadata table:
| Field | Example | Required? |
| team | eng-serving-runtime | yes |
| environment | prod | yes |
| metrics_namespace | redwood.runtime | yes |

4) Model-Serving Standards
Purpose: Ensure models are packaged, instrumented, and deployed safely and efficiently.
Rules:
- Model packaging: models must include model manifest (model.yaml) with metadata: name, version, architecture, tokenization, quantization options, input/output schema, and expected peak memory.
- Containerization: model server runtime should be reproducible with Docker image tagged by commit SHA and model version. Images stored in private registry with immutable tags.
- Config example (model.yaml):

name: redwood/gpt-medium
version: 2026-03-01
architecture: transformer
input_schema: text:string
output_schema: text:string
max_sequence_length: 4096
quantization_profiles: ["int8", "int4"]
recommended_batch_size: 8

- Rollouts & canarying: default rollout strategy for new model versions is a 10% canary for 24h, monitoring key metrics (latency p95, error rate, output-quality regressions). See rollout checklist below.
- Fallbacks: every serving route must declare compatible fallback model(s) and degrade gracefully with a 95th percentile response that indicates fallback used.
- KV cache & prefix caching: models should declare whether they support prefix/KV caching; runtime will honor caching configs set by serving teams.
- Quantization & performance profiles: maintain quantization-profiles directory; any quantization used in production must be validated by eval-harness with a quality regression tolerance (default 1% delta on specified evals).
- Model evals: include an eval suite (prompt sets and metrics) and acceptance criteria in PR for model onboarding.

Rollout checklist (numbered)
1. Create release artifact and tag image.
2. Run smoke tests in staging.
3. Deploy 10% canary for 24h.
4. Monitor latency p95, error rate, and quality evals.
5. If metrics are within thresholds, advance to 50% for 6h, then full rollout.
6. If regressions occur, trigger automatic rollback and open incident.

5) Observability Standards
Purpose: Make failures obvious and root cause analysis fast.
Core telemetry
- Metrics: instrumented metrics MUST include: request_count (by route/model), request_latency_ms (histogram), request_errors, model_cache_hit_rate, token_generation_rate.
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry is the standard. All services must propagate trace context and include trace IDs in logs.
- Logs: structured JSON logs with keys: timestamp, level, service, env, request_id, trace_id, model, route, message, error_code (if any).
- Dashboards & SLOs: teams must create per-service dashboards and SLO pages in eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts.

SLOs & alerting thresholds (baseline)
- API Gateway (hosted): availability 99.95% (monthly), latency p95 < 300ms for control-plane ops, error rate < 0.1%
- Inference serving (standard): availability 99.9% (monthly), latency p95 < 500ms for production routes, p99 < 2s for large sequences, token-generation throughput targets documented per-model.
- Model cold-start: 95% of model warmups must complete within 30s for common model sizes (<= 8B parameters).

Alerting guidelines
- High-priority alerts: SLO breach projection, incident-level increases in 5xx rate (>1% sustained 5min), autoscaler thrashing, cluster OOMs. Pager duty escalation for Sev2/Sev1.
- Noise reduction: prefer aggregated alerts and dynamic thresholds; use suppression windows for planned maintenance.

6) Performance Standards & Benchmarking
Purpose: Ensure predictable performance and capacity planning for serving workloads.
Rules & process:
- Benchmark harness: services must include reproducible perf tests under eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite using standard workloads.
- Key perf metrics: tokens/sec per GPU, p50/p95/p99 latency per sequence length, memory usage at peak, and KV cache hit improvement.
- Resource sizing: use historical load + 2x safety margin for autoscaler thresholds; document assumptions in runbooks.
- Continuous perf regression detection: CI pipeline will run lightweight perf checks on PRs that touch runtime or model changes; full-suite nightly job compares to baseline.

Benchmark example table:
| Model | GPU type | batch size | tokens/sec | p95 latency | notes |
| redwood/gpt-medium | A100-80GB | 8 | 12,000 | 420ms | int8 quantized |

Decision Records / ADRs
- All non-trivial architecture decisions must have an ADR in the repo under docs/adrs with the following fields: ADR-ID, title, context, decision, consequences, date, authors.
- Example ADR summaries (these should link to full ADRs):
  - ADR-2026-01: "Standardize API Versioning" — decision to use major-segment versioning and OpenAPI published per-service.
  - ADR-2026-03: "Default Model Quantization Policy" — decide int8 as default for production-facing medium models with eval constraints.
  - ADR-2026-07: "Service Mesh vs Sidecar Tracing" — choose lightweight sidecar-instrumented tracing using OpenTelemetry collectors.

Operational Playbooks & Runbooks
- Each service must have a runbook with: owner, on-call rotation, common failure modes, escalations, rollback procedures, and links to dashboards. Store runbooks under eng-platform/runbooks or service repo in /docs/runbook.md.

Compliance & Security Notes
- Data residency: model artifacts and logs must respect customer-configured residency; use region tags and separate storage buckets for restricted deployments.
- Audit logging: all control-plane changes must be audit-logged to an immutable store with retention policy per compliance guide.
- RBAC: use least-privilege IAM roles; service accounts must have narrow scopes and short-lived credentials when possible.

Onboarding & Exceptions
- New projects must follow the New Service checklist: API design review, security review, infra module checklist, observability dashboard, and runbook before production traffic.
- Exceptions: documented exceptions can be requested via a change-management ticket and must include compensating controls and an owner.

Related pages
- architecture-and-standards/api-standards (OpenAPI conventions and examples)
- eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite (bench harness)
- applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles (profile catalog)
- policies-and-process/change-management (change approval)
- eng-platform/runbooks (runbook templates)

Appendix: Short checklist for PR reviewers
- API: OpenAPI spec updated, non-breaking change, idempotency considered.
- Security: no secrets, vault integration for creds, dependency scan passed.
- Observability: metrics and tracing added, logs structured.
- Tests: unit and integration tests added, perf checks when relevant.
- Infra: terraform plan included and reviewed, tagging and metrics outputs present.

This document will be reviewed quarterly and after any major platform change. For questions or to propose edits, open a PR against this document or contact the standards owner.
